question.text:
Insertion of a new element into an AVL tree may violate the AVL balance condition. Usually, we perform a rotation at the first node on the path from the inserted element to the root that violates the AVL balance condition.

What would happen if we instead choose the first node on the path from the root to the inserted element that violates the AVL balance condition?

  1. After the rotation, at least one node will always still violate the balance condition, so another rotation will always be necessary.
     
  2. The entire AVL tree will be balanced after the rotation, but more nodes may be changed by the rotation.
     
  3. The entire AVL tree will be balanced after the rotation, and the same number of nodes will be changed.
     
  4. The entire AVL tree will be balanced after the rotation, and the same number or fewer nodes may be changed.
     
  5. The entire AVL tree may or may not be balanced after the rotation.
